items.title: Elden Ring Director Hidetaka Miyazaki Says He's 'Honestly Not Sure' Where the Rumor About Him Having a Foot Fetish Came From
items.description: Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki has addressed the rumors that he's got a foot fetish, and he seemed pretty baffled by the whole thing.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki has addressed the rumors that he's got a foot fetish, and he seemed pretty baffled by the whole thing.

Miyazaki’s games are beloved for their brutal gameplay, grimdark settings, and tortured characters. Of these characters, several of the female bosses, NPCs, and helpers share a common trait: They aren’t wearing any shoes.

The Maiden in Black from Demons’ Souls, Sister Friede, Gwunevere, and Priscilla from the Dark Souls games, and even Malenia in Elden Ring all boast bare feet. (Yes, we know Malenia’s legs were destroyed by the Scarlet Rot, but her brother created prosthetics for her that included highly-detailed feet with individual toes. That still counts!)

Over the years, this has sparked an inside joke within the Soulslike community, who lightheartedly figured that Miyazaki must be a foot guy. It was never a serious thing — but he brought it up, totally unprompted, during an interview with The Guardian in September 2026.

Miyazaki was responding to a question about recurring imagery of hands that crops up across most of his games, including his most recent offering, The Duskbloods.

“It’s not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of – maybe it’s something subconscious coming through,” he answered. “Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from. I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe.”

Hey, we’re not gonna yuck anyone’s yum, but it sounds like this wasn’t even a thought in Miyazaki’s mind when he made these character designs. Instead, he was trying to depict some kind of overarching symbolism about humanity within those characters’ appearances, which includes themes like “ruin and rebirth.”

“[Ruin and rebirth] is an ongoing theme in a lot of my games, I realise,” he added in his interview with The Guardian. “That theme on a cosmological scale applies to The Duskbloods as an interesting philosophical area to explore.

“If we have two ideas of a brighter or dark future, I would tend to sway towards the darker one,” Miyazaki says. “[But] if you explore the ruin and the decay in those worlds, it also lets you explore some chance of rebirth, and I think having that tiny pinprick of light or hope can be something beautiful, something fleeting,” he continued.

Speaking of The Duskbloods, IGN’s Michael Higham described the upcoming title as “FromSoftware’s most complex and interesting game yet” in his hands-on preview. In the lead-up to its launch, he also got the chance to chat with Miyazaki about the game, who told us a bit more about its development process and assured us that yes, Fromsoft is still interested in making single-player games.

items.title: Turkish GTA 6 Fans Want Language Support So Badly, They Professionally Dubbed the Gameplay Reveal
items.description: Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub the game's gameplay reveal.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub its gameplay reveal.

The Turkish gaming community has been asking for more and more studios to add Turkish language support for their games. This has led to massive fan campaigns for titles like 007 First Light, which actually resulted in IO Interactive adding Turkish subtitles to the game. Now, the Turkish gaming community is turning their focus to the most anticipated release of the year, if not the most anticipated game in history: Grand Theft Auto 6.

Fans have been asking Rockstar Games to add Turkish subtitles or voice overs to GTA 6 ahead of its release in November. They aren't just making social media posts tagging Rockstar, either; they actually professionally dubbed and mixed the entire GTA 6 extended look with a whole cast of actors. The Turkish dub went up just a day after the gameplay was released, which means there was a very fast turn around. It's pretty impressive and shows, there are members of the community actively trying to make this a reality.

YouTuber Pintipanda also made a video asking Rockstar to see the potential in localizing GTA 6 for Turkish players. In it, he points out how Turkish-speaking individuals exist in a number of countries outside of Turkey itself, and that GTA 6 is bound to have a wide reach, so it should be as inclusive as possible.

"I know that you guys do these things internally, but if creating a team from zero is hard or you don't have the time or the luxury, you have the money, of course. There is an alternative way to do this. We have world-class Turkish localization teams here. We are playing The Witcher 3 in Turkish, Cyberpunk 2077 in Turkish, Baldur's Gate in Turkish, and Warhammer games in Turkish. As you guessed, these are text-heavy games that we are playing and enjoy in our native country.

"The studios behind these games like CD Projekt Red or Techland, all the studios are getting their investment back with the sales. That's a win-win, that's an alternative way to do these kinds of things. The choice is yours."

The creator went on to say he's aware that localizing GTA 6 won't happen overnight, but the community simply wants to be acknowledged by Rockstar as a "starting point." Ultimately, we'll just have to wait and see what happens, but it's clear there is a passionate group of players trying to get the best experience for themselves.

GTA 6 is a little more than two months away now, and Rockstar has its foot on the gas when it comes to marketing. Following the gameplay reveal last week, a bunch of previews of GTA 6 were released from select content creators and IGN itself. This has resulted in no shortage of news and details about the highly-anticipated game. Earlier today, Rockstar and PlayStation also revealed two limited-edition GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers, which will go up for pre-order next week.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 Is Bringing Back a Major Dead Character in an Unexpected Way
items.description: Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spoilers for Dexter: Resurrection Season 1 and seemingly Season 2 follow below.

Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died.

Deadline has reported that Angel Batista, played by David Zayas, will return in the next season of Dexter: Resurrection. Batista has been in every single season of Dexter in some form since the very beginning, but he met an unfortunate end in Season 1 of Resurrection. After trying to bring Dexter to justice, he ended up being shot and killed by the season's antagonist, Leon Prater. It was a tragic conclusion to the character's arc and one that punished Dexter for trying to have it all.

However, Batista will be back once again in Season 2. The actor was seen on set filming a scene with Michael C. Hall in Times Square. Interestingly, he was sporting a more colorful outfit than the last time we saw him, with a Hawaiian shirt, his signature hat, and his gun holster. This seems to suggest that Zayas is returning as one of Dexter's ghosts, preserved in an outfit from when he was a detective in Florida. Various characters have appeared after their deaths to guide or antagonize Dexter over the course of the franchise, but they're not literal ghosts. They're more like manifestations of Dexter's conscience, so Batista may represent some kind of internal guilt for the titular serial killer this time around.

His inclusion makes sense, especially as Joey Quinn, another cop from Dexter's past, will also return this season. It's unclear how that story will unravel, but hopefully the writers are smart enough to recognize they can't repeat Batista's arc with another Miami Metro detective. Either way, it seems like we're in for another suspenseful season of Dexter.

Batista also isn't the only dead character returning in Dexter: Resurrection, but the other one may not be as dead as we thought. We won't spoil it here, but you can click here for more details. Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is expected to premiere sometime this fall.

items.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's Most Popular Mod Completely Defeats the Purpose of the Game
items.description: The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a time-altering mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, a new RPG from ex-CD Projekt Red staff, the player fills the shoes of a man-turned-vampire who has 30 days to save his family. The game has a non-linear story with different approaches, allowing you to progress how you see fit, but there's a catch: Every mission you take on advances the game's 30-day clock. Some quests advance the clock more than others, forcing the player to be thoughtful about quests they accept. Character progression, such as using the skill tree, also advances the clock.

Naturally, some fans don't like the pressure this creates. The clock forces them to make tough decisions; it means you have to be choosey about what you do in the game. With that said, it makes sense that its most popular mod completely removes the tension created by this mechanic. The Better Story Timer mod on NexusMods gives you 90 days to do quests, triple the intended amount. This means you don't really have to be precious about the in-game clock or think too hard about your choices. It removes most, if not all, of the friction in The Blood of Dawnwalker.

Of course, something like this might make sense a couple of months post-release for those who want to play it differently, but it literally just came out today. The mod has been downloaded almost 10,000 times already, meaning it's pretty popular... but some users have expressed annoyance over players not giving the game a chance in the way it was intended.

"Gamers will do anything they can to not experience a game the way the developers intended," said one X/Twitter user. "I think the main issue is that, nowadays, gamers believe every game should be made for them. The issue is that’s rarely the case, and the games that do cater for everyone usually suck. Sometimes, you aren’t the target audience. And that’s perfectly fine."

The Blood of Dawnwalker is intended to be the beginning of a franchise, one that will sprawl across multiple eras, possibly including the modern day based on a previous trailer for the game. It's unclear when future entires will arrive, but currently, The Blood of Dawnwalker is being hailed as a strong RPG in reviews and appears to be off to a strong start commercially.

IGN gave it a 9/10 in its review, praising the inclusion of the in-game clock.

"The Blood of Dawnwalker is my new favorite vampire game and one of the best story-driven RPGs I’ve played in a long time," reads an excerpt from the review. "The day/night cycle that has you juggling human and vampiric forms is awesome, and the constraints placed on how you spend your limited time ends up being one of the coolest, most wonderfully stressful parts of the adventure."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Netflix Is Making a Live-Action Dungeons & Dragons Series About Darklord Strahd Von Zarovich's Origin Story
items.description: Netflix is cooking up a live-action Dungeons & Dragons TV show based on the tabletop RPG’s gothic-horror campaign, Ravenloft, and its vampire villain, Darklord Strahd von Zarovich.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Netflix is cooking up a live-action Dungeons & Dragons TV show based on the tabletop RPG’s gothic-horror campaign, Ravenloft, and its vampire villain, Darklord Strahd von Zarovich.

The spooky series is penned as an origin story that dives into the events that turned Zarovitch into the vicious vampire count we all know and love today.

As told by Variety, Netflix’s Ravenloft show is described as a “prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance.”

“Ravenloft and its Domains of Dread redefine adventure through character-driven stories of dark magic and supernatural intrigue. At the heart of the series, Ravenloft follows the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, whose story of power, love, obsession, and undead transformation charts his origins from tragic antihero to one of Dungeons & Dragons’ most notorious villains,” the description reads.

The series is created by John August (co-host of scriptwriting podcast Scriptnotes, Corpse Bride, Charlie and the Chocolate Factory) and is being executive produced by Alfonso Cuarón, Hasbro’s Gabriel Marano, Richard Schwartz, and Esperanto Filmoj’s Gaby Rodriguez.

Strahd von Zarovich is very much a Dracula-inspired character; formerly a prince and warlord, he got anxious in his middle age and made a pact with the Dark Powers to gain immortality. Part of that pact involved killing his own brother so he might marry his wife (Zarovich’s sister-in-law). However, it’s safe to say that she was not into her brother-in-law, as she literally flung herself off of a cliff to get away from him, killing herself and leaving Zarovich heartbroken.

This isn’t the only exciting news for D&D fans; a new game from the franchise was shown off at gamescom this year called Dungeons & Dragons: Warlock, starring Tricia Helfer as Kaatri, a warlock, and Maggie Robertson (Resident Evil Village’s Lady Dimitrescu) as Tasha, a powerful witch-queen and Kaatri’s patron.

News of Netflix’s forthcoming show follows Wizards of the Coast’s April 2026 release of Ravenloft: The Horrors Within expansion, which gave players an updated version of the original story as part of Dungeons & Dragons’ Season of Horror event.

On the flip side, Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves directors John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein are still holding out hope for a sequel after Paramount passed on the project due to “financial” reasons. While it wasn’t a box office hit at the time, fans have come to love the fantasy flick in the years since then, and with Netflix cooking up a live-action show, the D&D universe is looking like an exciting brand for studios to back.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Blizzard Might Be Teasing a New StarCraft Game
items.description: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game?
items.author: Bo Moore
items.content:
There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game?

That would make sense. A report earlier this year said that Blizzard had partnered with Korean gaming giant Nexon to develop a new StarCraft shooter. Blizzard declined to comment on the matter at the time, and the partnership remains unconfirmed, but a report yesterday from South Korean newspaper Chosun (via Wccftech) reaffirms that Nexon is seeking a license to develop a new StarCraft game.

Meanwhile, Blizzard may have been working on its own new StarCraft game, as per a 2024 job posting for an "upcoming open-world shooter." Reports from that time suggested the title was in development at Blizzard, led by former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined the company in 2022.

Another point of evidence is that BlizzCon returns on September 12 after a three-year hiatus, and Blizzard will undoubtedly want to make a splash there with big news beyond its ongoing franchises. There's also a conspicuous hour-long gap on BlizzCon's day-one mainstage programming, while all other panels only have 15 minutes of downtime between them. Sure seems like the place for something that gets announced during the opening ceremonies.

StarCraft as a franchise has sat dormant since 2017's remaster of the original game, which will celebrate its 30th anniversary in 2028. StarCraft 2 launched in 2010, with its subsequent expansions concluding in 2015. Meanwhile, legendary vaporware third-person shooter StarCraft: Ghost was announced in 2002 and eventually confirmed to be cancelled in 2014.

I can't verify exactly how long the glitch effect on the StarCraft website has been live, but I haven't seen anyone talking about it yet, and the most recent Wayback Machine capture of the page from just over a week ago doesn't show the effect (though I can't be sure if the Wayback Machine would properly capture and show it).

It's unclear if this tease is related to Blizzard's own game, the one from the Nexon partnership, if those two games are one in the same, if either of them are StarCraft 3, or none of the above. IGN has reached out to Blizzard for comment on both the tease and the Nexon partnership, and will update this article if we hear back.

Either way, BlizzCon is just over a week away, so a formal announcement could be just on the horizon.

Bo Moore is IGN's Senior Manager of Tech. You can find him online @usebomswisely.

Another point of evidence is that BlizzCon returns on September 12 after a three-year hiatus, and Blizzard will undoubtedly want to make a splash there with big news beyond its ongoing franchises. There's also a conspicuous hour-long gap on BlizzCon's day-one mainstage programming, while all other panels only have 15 minutes of downtime between them. Sure seems like the place for something that gets announced during the opening ceremonies.

StarCraft as a franchise has sat dormant since 2017's remaster of the original game, which will celebrate its 30th anniversary in 2028. StarCraft 2 launched in 2010, with its subsequent expansions concluding in 2015. Meanwhile, legendary vaporware third-person shooter StarCraft: Ghost was announced in 2002 and eventually confirmed to be cancelled in 2014.

I can't verify exactly how long the glitch effect on the StarCraft website has been live, but I haven't seen anyone talking about it yet, and the most recent Wayback Machine capture of the page from just over a week ago doesn't show the effect (though I can't be sure if the Wayback Machine would properly capture and show it).

It's unclear if this tease is related to Blizzard's own game, the one from the Nexon partnership, if those two games are one in the same, if either of them are StarCraft 3, or none of the above. IGN has reached out to Blizzard for comment on both the tease and the Nexon partnership, and will update this article if we hear back.

items.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves Directors Say Film Flopped Due to 'Not-So-Great' Timing
items.description: The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes.

Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves released in March 2023, right around the time that Wizards of the Coast was facing massive backlash from players after confirming planned adjustments to their Open-Gaming License that would have made sweeping changes to rules that allowed creators to make and sell their own content based on the tabletop RPG’s fifth edition.

While they ultimately ended up walking this disastrous decision back, the blowback was enough to negatively impact the movie adaptation, says director John Francis Daley. He claims that this drama, alongside the hugely-successful launch of The Super Mario Bros. Movie around the same time, ultimately overshadowed a film that has since proven to be a hit among fans after the fact.

“It was very much a product of not-so-great timing when the first movie came out,” Daley said in an episode of The Discourse Podcast. “It came out four days before the Super Mario movie, which broke records. It came out a month after Wizards of the Coast changed the official gaming license, prompting many D&D fans to boycott the game, and I don’t think the marketing did enough to tell people who weren’t already fans that this movie might be for them. Yeah, so it was a perfect storm of all of those elements, and we’ll see.”

Honor Among Thieves struggled at the box office, and Paramount has since passed up on making a sequel due to “financial” reasons. But Daley and Goldstein are hopeful that another studio will pick them up to continue telling stories in the Dungeons & Dragons universe.

“Yeah, absolutely,” Goldstein confirmed after being asked if anyone is actively crunching the numbers for a possible sequel. “I think Hasbro is a big believer in it, and if they can figure out a studio partner to make it work, they’ll want to proceed. As are our producers.”

“I mean, look, it’s something that is near and dear to our hearts in that we loved making the first one,” Daley added. “We fell in love with the characters, and there’s so much potential in a sequel because the first act isn’t filled with exposition or introduction to this family that we’ve already become accustomed to. So you can kind of launch right into the story, which is really nice.”

Fans shouldn’t despair; while an Honor Among Thieves sequel is still up in the air, a live-action TV series is officially in the works at Netflix, based on the TTRPG’s gothic-horror world “Ravenloft.” Described as a “prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance,” it follows “the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovic.”

Even better, a new third-person action-adventure game titled Dungeons & Dragons: Warlock is also in development, set to release sometime in 2027.

items.title: Miami-Dade Sheriff and Commissioner Slam City's Proposed GTA 6 Takeover for 'Promoting Fictional Version of Our Community Defined by Crime and Violence'
items.description: The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement.

Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, Florida. Rockstar took pains to faithfully recreate Miami’s most iconic locales and architecture within the game, with fans already spotting a few real-life locations in the title’s newest trailers.

In late August, local news outlets reported that Miami-Dade County officials had spoken with Rockstar Games about potential plans for a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami, which included ideas like wrapping the Metro line with Vice City branding, creating Vice City manhole covers, and decking out the Miami International Airport with ‘Welcome to Vice City’ signage.

While nothing has been formally approved, it seemed like the city was gung-ho for a partnership with the biggest game of the year… but now, the Miami-Dade county sheriff is bringing those ideas to a screeching halt.

Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz and Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez believe that celebrating Grand Theft Auto — a game series famous for allowing players to engage in criminal activity — in such a way would essentially promot a fictionalized, crime-ridden version of their city.

"Grand Theft Auto is a video game franchise built around criminal activity. Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office work every single day to prevent," Cordero-Stutz said, per NBC Miami 6.

"At a time when law enforcement is working every day to reduce violent crime, prevent robberies and car thefts, combat drug trafficking, and build stronger relationships between our deputies and the communities we serve, I believe we need to seriously consider the message we send when our own government promotes a fictional identity centered around many of those same crimes."

“I still cannot believe that we are even considering temporarily rebranding important County assets, including Miami International Airport, as 'Vice City Airport,'" Bermudez added. "Miami-Dade County has spent decades building a reputation as a world-class destination for tourism, business, investment, and opportunity. We should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence."

It’s unclear what the future of Miami’s GTA 6 takeover will look like, now that the county sheriff has spoken out against the idea… but with the title shaping up to be one of the biggest releases in video game history, it certainly seems like a profitable venture, should it actually work out.

The sheriff isn't the only one balking at GTA 6's November 19 launch; spouses across social media have also kicked off a heated debate after claiming that playing the game, which features a relationship mechanic between dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, is tantamount to cheating.

items.title: Brandon Sanderson Makes the Case for Reading the Project Hail Mary Book Even If You've Seen the Movie Already
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
Since revealing his new relationship with Hollywood, Brandon Sanderson's weekly podcast has become increasingly focused on movie and book adaptations. This week, he and his co-host Dan Wells dove into the topic of the Project Hail Mary movie, and Sanderson makes a compelling case for reading Andy Weir's book.

"They left out a lot of the science, the try fails, the figuring out how everything works," Sanderson said. He went on to explain that the moment he finds out he's on a spaceship is quite a bit longer in the books compared to the movie, describing the experience as if "you're figuring it out with him, like what is this? What is going on?"

Sanderson still had nothing but positive things to say about the film, saying he thinks "they did a fantastic job." IGN's review of the film reflects his same sentiment, which landed it on our list of the top-reviewed movies of 2026 so far.

What we said in our movie review

"Thrilling, heartfelt, and hilarious, Project Hail Mary is a rollicking sci-fi blockbuster. Lord and Miller faithfully adapt Andy Weir’s novel, carrying forward the author’s celebration of science, teamwork, and bravery on a huge scale, bolstered by great performances from Ryan Gosling and James Ortiz and Greig Fraser’s fantastic work behind the camera. Some pacing issues inherent in closely adapting the novel’s structure do make for a somewhat rough landing, but through the lens of Grace and Rocky’s partnership being the real mission we want to see succeed, Project Hail Mary is a memorable celebration of how much we can accomplish when we work together." - Tom Jorgensen

As someone who read the book before watching the movie, I definitely agree with Sanderson on this topic. Movies are never going to be able to provide the same level of depth you're going to get from the novel. Andy Weir is great about taking you on a fun journey of details, but a film can't truly show all of that. When you're dealing with a limited runtime, all you can do is enough to make the science feel believable as a plot device. In the books, you get to really dig deep into what the character is experiencing in every scene.

For those who haven't read the book, I highly recommend it. It's one of those books that really puts the science in science-fiction in the best way possible. It's also one of my favorite audiobooks. Narrator Ray Porter has an incredibly soothing voice and there are some excellent background sounds that really sell the audio experience. It's an easy transition coming from the movie if you're not used to reading books.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics -- from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets.

items.title: Waffle House Movie in the Works Starring X-Men’s Inde Navarrette
items.description: Not content just to appear in Marvel's X-Men reboot, Inde Navarrette has signed on to star in a bizarre sci-fi thriller called The Waffle House Index.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Obsession star Inde Navarrette may have just signed on for Marvel's upcoming X-Men reboot, but that's not stopping her from taking on smaller and weirder projects. Case in point: Navarrette is slated to star in The Waffle House Index, a sci-fi thriller about a Waffle House waitress dealing with an overnight shift from hell.

The news comes courtesy of The Hollywood Reporter. THR writes that the film has just been picked up by Apple Original Films. It features a screenplay by Andrew Nunnelly, one that was featured on the 2025 Black List (a list of the most acclaimed unproduced scripts circulating in Hollywood). The Waffle House Index is slated to be directed by Louis Paxton (The Incomer). The film will be produced by Plan B Entertainment, with Navarrette herself executive producing.

The title of the film refers to the infamous barometer Waffle House restaurants use while under hurricane threat. A Waffle House Index can range from green to yellow to red depending on how severe weather conditions are and whether a given restaurant stays open or not. In short, if the Waffle House Index is red, it's time to panic.

The index may well reach the red zone in this movie, as it's teased that Navarrette's beleaguered character will deal with everything from a rogue gunman to flash floods to crocodile attacks to nuclear missiles and even a hidden bunker located underneath the Waffle House itself (hey, it is a sci-fi movie).

Alongside X-Men, this marks the first new project for Navarrette following her breakout performance in 2026's Obsession. In IGN's Obsession review, Matt Donato writes, "Obsession should and will put Barker on the map as a horror filmmaker you need to watch. Thanks to fantastic turns by Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, you'll be addicted to this sour Valentine's Day counterprogramming. The film plays on familiar romance and monkey's paw tropes, turning a wish against the wishee, but Barker's execution takes things to the next level. In the film's simplicity lay the chance to go for broke, putting all efforts into the lengths Nikki is willing to go for her beloved. With that focus and Barker's fearlessness, Obsession becomes one hell of a maximalist ride."

For more on the new X-Men movie, find out why Wolverine isn't needed in the reboot.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky.

items.title: YouTube Star MoistCr1TiKaL Is Making a Full-Length Animated Movie Based on His Godslap Comic, Coming to Theaters in 2028
items.description: YouTube star Charlie ‘MoistCr1tikal’ White is the mastermind behind a full-length animated movie adaptation of his very own comic, Godslap, set to release in theaters in 2028.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
YouTube star Charles ‘MoistCr1TiKaL’ White is the mastermind behind a full-length animated movie adaptation of his very own comic, Godslap, set to release in theaters in 2028.

The film’s first teaser trailer was published on September 3, 2026, showing off the slick animation and smooth artwork from Powerhouse Animation, best known for its work on Netflix’s Castlevania: Nocturne and Masters of the Universe: Revelation.

As told by White in a YouTube video announcing the news, the Godslap movie follows Aius, a young man with the “incredibly strong gift of slapping.” However, his incredible power has made his father, Darius, extremely overprotective of him, fearing what could happen if he were to venture into the outside world.

First teaser for ‘GODSLAP’, a new animated film based on MoistCr1TiKaL's comic series.

The film follows a boy with an extraordinary slapping ability who ventures out into the world for the first time. pic.twitter.com/RfrajR1SuY

— DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) September 3, 2026

“He is now, for the first time, venturing out from his farm where his father Darius has been kind of an overbearing a**hole trying to keep him away from the rest of the world out of fear for what that power could do,” White explained.

The YouTuber revealed that he first approached Powerhouse Animation about the project all the way back in 2018. At the time, however, he was unprepared for the sheer amount of money it’d take to finance such a venture and effectively ghosted the studio, resigning himself to the reality that his dream of adapting Godslap into an animated movie might be too expensive to ever realize.

Years passed… but three years ago, Powerhouse reached out to White saying they were interested in adapting the comic, which is still roughly two years away from being fully finished.

White says that he plans on releasing the movie in theaters, making it the second big influencer-led project to have a theatrical release following Markiplier’s indie horror Iron Lung earlier this year.

White said that he is the “sole financier” of the Godslap movie, and that he and the team behind the comic have been “involved every single step of the way.”

“This has been one of the biggest dreams I’ve had since I was a child, and I believe in it so strongly that I’ve been putting my money where my c**k is — millions, in order to bring this project to life and make it as big, as special, as unique as it can possibly be,” he said.

The YouTuber plans on sharing more information in the coming months, including voice talent, behind-the-scenes info, and more.

Speaking with Deadline, Lyrical Animation's Creative Director, Daniel Dominguez, said the studio, which is co-developing the Godslap movie alongside Powerhouse, have been fans of White for a long time.

“Getting the opportunity to bring his anime-inflected, hilariously violent comic Godslap to life was a dream come true,” he said. “It’s one of the funniest, most non-stop surprising, and thematically urgent comics to come out in the last decade, and a perfect story to adapt as an animated feature.”

White has been involved in quite a few animated projects himself prior to the Godslap movie; gamers will recognize him as the voice of Sonar id Adhoc’s Dispatch, and anime fans might remember that he voiced a character in Netflix’s Baki series.

items.title: Until Dawn 2 Was Co-Developed by Dispatch Developer AdHoc Studio
items.description: AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptached, helped develop Until Dawn 2.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptach, helped develop Until Dawn 2.

In a new PlayStation Blog post, Until Dawn 2 developer Firesprite confirmed that AdHoc helped craft the story of the new horror game. As a result, the team promises a much richer experience with tough choices that impact the branching narrative.

"We’ve partnered with our friends at AdHoc Studio – the brilliant minds behind the acclaimed Dispatch – so you can expect a deeply layered story packed with rich characters, razor-sharp dialogue, fraught relationships, tough decisions, and yes… more than a few gruesome deaths," reads the post. "Every choice, every interaction can ripple with dramatic consequences."

AdHoc has been around for nearly a decade, but only released its first game last year. The team is largely comprised of ex-Telltale, Ubisoft, and Night School Studio talent, which has allowed them to use their narrative expertise for new titles like Dispatch. The 2025 superhero game was a refreshing experience take on a tried and true genre with nuanced relationships, hilarious and compelling writing, and meaningful choices.

Given AdHoc only rose to prominence last year, it's unclear when they were brought on to Until Dawn 2. They could've been a late addition to punch up the game following the success of Dispatch, or Firesprite could've recognized their potential early on and brought them in a couple of years ago. Either way, it's great to see the AdHoc team being utilized on a franchise that means so much to horror fans.

Firesprite also announced that Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January, which is sooner than some would've anticipated. The game was announced earlier this summer and will feature returning characters, such as the mysterious Dr. Hill, from the first game.

items.title: Naughty Dog 'Not Done' With The Last of Us, but Studio Not Involved With HBO Show's 3rd Season
items.description: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann says that neither he nor the studio are involved with the third season of the HBO TV adaptation of the beloved video game, but says that the developer "isn't done" with the franchise yet.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann says that neither he nor the studio are involved with the third season of the HBO TV adaptation of the beloved video game, but says that the developer "isn't done" with the franchise yet.

Speaking to The Washington Post, Druckmann said, "I wasn't involved in shaping this season's creative direction, and Naughty Dog did not have a creative role in the direction of this season. So I can't personally speak to how production is progressing." He then pretty clearly suggested that Naughty Dog will take on future projects in The Last of Us universe, though whether that's a proper The Last of Us Part 3, a resurrection of the canceled The Last of Us Online multiplayer project, or something else remains to be seen. "It's important for us to note that as the creator of the games, Naughty Dog is still the steward of this IP and even though this might be the end of this adaptation," he added, referring to the HBO show's third season, "we're not done with The Last of Us. There's a couple projects in the works that, when the time is right, I'm very excited to talk about."

Naughty Dog is currently focused on its next game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, which was a no-show at today's Sony State of Play, but did recently wrap cinematic shooting. It does not yet have a release window.

On The Last of Us TV show, meanwhile, Peter Sarsgaard has been cast in a role for an original character not featured in the games, while Li Jun Li was cast as Miriam, among numerous other cast announcements. We also recently learned that Matthew McConaughey turned down the part of Joel, which of course went to Pedro Pascal.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Supergirl Is Coming to HBO Max Next Week
items.description: Supergirl officially has a streaming release date.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Supergirl officially has a streaming release date.

The latest movie from James Gunn’s DC reboot will be available to HBO Max subscribers starting next Thursday, September 10. An ASL Version of the film will be available at the same time, and it will debut on HBO linear the following day, September 11, at 8pm ET.

Starring Milly Alcock in the titular role, Supergirl is the second major movie in the new DC Universe helmed by James Gunn, following up on last year’s Superman. Unfortunately, it struggled to match its predecessor’s run at the box office.

Where Superman quickly soared to over $600 million globally, Supergirl struggled from its opening weekend. The film ended its run in theaters with a worldwide gross of just over $126 million on a budget Variety reported as somewhere between $170 and $185 million.

Unfortunately, the film hasn’t fared too well on the critical side, either. Supergirl currently sits at a 53% score on Rotten Tomatoes. Critic Clint Gage reviewed the movie for IGN, saying "Milly Alcock’s great take on Kara Zor-El gets lost in the spare parts from other movies used to assemble her story."

The arrival on HBO Max follows the film’s release on digital earlier this month and will also follow a DVD release, which includes a limited edition 4K steelbook, on September 8.

DC Studios co-head Peter Safran has spoken on the film’s box office performance in an interview with The New York Times: "While Supergirl didn’t meet our box office expectations, it’s just one component of a broader, long-term strategy at DC Studios that we remain confident in." We also recently learned that the movie had competing cuts, reportedly in part due to creative differences between Gunn and director Craig Gillespie.

Supergirl's poor box office performance put even more pressure on DC's subsequent project, Lanterns. The live action series is currently releasing new episodes on HBO Max, and we've been pretty big fans of the first season. Viewership seems to be looking pretty good so far, too.

Going forward, Gunn himself is fully focused on the Superman follow-up, Man of Tomorrow. DC Studios will get another big movie in theaters before then, though: Clayface, a live-action body horror take on the Batman villain, is slated for release this October. Speaking of Batman, we finally got a teaser for the Matt Reeves sequel.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: New Dave Bautista Video Reveals He's Putting On a Ton of Muscle to Play Kratos in God of War
items.description: Dave Bautista has posted a new video showing his body transformation for Kratos in the new God of War TV series.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Dave Bautista has posted a new video showing his body transformation for Kratos in the new God of War TV show.

Bautista was officially cast as Kratos in the God of War TV series last month and he has wasted no time prepping for the role. The actor shared a video on Instagram flexing his new physique, noting that he has been weight training for three weeks and has two months to "get to where he needs to be."

Unlike other roles where an actor might have six to twelve months or more to prepare, Bautista has to hit the ground running. The God of War TV series began shooting earlier this year with actor Ryan Hurst in the role of Kratos. Unfortunately, Hurst got injured (after also putting in the work at the gym for the role) and will be out of commission until next year. Amazon made the decision to recast the role and quickly hired Dave Bautista, who now has just a couple of months to get into Kratos-level shape. The show is expected to restart production in October, meaning Bautista won't have much time to rest.

The actor had recently lost a ton of weight and muscle after years of starring in action movies and being a professional wrestler. While Bautsita made sense as Kratos five years ago, some began to question if he was the right choice due to him being much slimmer. Bautista seems to be interested in proving the naysayers wrong and is hitting the weight room to get real beefy before stepping into the shoes of a gaming god.

Christopher Judge, the actor who plays Kratos in the current God of War games, revealed he auditioned to play the character in live-action. However, he ultimately took himself out of the running because he didn't want to work 12 - 18 hour days, have an intense diet, or work out constantly at 62 years old.

(Photo by Gilbert Flores/Penske Media via Getty Images)

items.title: The Odyssey Is Extending Its IMAX 70MM Run Once Again Through the End of September
items.description: If you have yet to see the Odyssey in IMAX 70MM or need an excuse to watch it again, showtimes for Christopher Nolan's epic at 39 theaters worldwide that support the much-desired format have been extended through September 30, 2026.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
If you have yet to see the Odyssey in IMAX 70MM or need an excuse to watch it again, showtimes for Christopher Nolan's epic at 39 theaters worldwide that support the much-desired format have been extended through September 30, 2026.

The Odyssey's historic IMAX run was supposed to end on September 15, but the "overwhelming public demand" behind this decision will now see the film staying in the format it's "intended" to be seen for 11 weeks.

If you want to see it for yourself, check out the showtimes right here.

Since it first premiered on July 17, The Odyssey has become the highest-grossing IMAX release of all time, earning $457 million at the global box office. The IMAX 70MM screenings alone have accounted for $66 million of that across the 41 theaters that feature it. These accolades are fitting, as The Odyssey was also the first film to ever be shot entirely with IMAX cameras.

Per Box Office Mojo, The Odyssey has surpassed $1.55 billion at the global box office and will look to extend that run over the course of September as it races toward $2 billion.

In our The Odyssey review, we said that it "adapts Homer through a new eye that brings a sense of horror and existential angst to the story – and some humor too. It may not be a perfect movie, but it’s a pretty great moviegoing experience all the same."

For more, check out our explainer of the ending of The Odyssey, Nolan's long and winding road to this film, and why its scariest scene proves it's time for a Nolan horror movie.

items.title: Microsoft Announces Big Changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming, Switches to Monthly Hour Limits
items.description: Microsoft has announced big changes to Xbox cloud gaming, including a switch to monthly hour limits.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft has announced big changes to Xbox cloud gaming, including a switch to monthly hour limits.

From November, Game Pass plans will include a set number of cloud gaming hours each month:

Xbox Game Pass cloud gaming monthly limits:

  • Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours
  • Game Pass Premium: 10 hours
  • Game Pass Essential: 5 hours

Once subscribers use their included hours, they can buy additional cloud playtime through the Xbox Store. Currently, Game Pass subscribers can stream without these monthly hour limits. The change means those who use cloud gaming most via Game Pass will end up having to pay more, although Microsoft said this impacts 4% of Game Pass subscribers.

Also in November, Microsoft said players will be able to buy cloud playtime hours through the Xbox Store and ‘stream eligible games they own on supported devices’ without subscribing to Game Pass.

In a blog post, Microsoft said it was making the changes because the cost of providing cloud gaming has grown as more people use it and play for longer. The monthly limits, Microsoft continued, will mean it can invest in reliability and performance. But it said it understood that for some players the practical result is a higher cost.

Expect more information on pricing, purchasing additional hours, eligible games, market availability, and how players can check their remaining time in November. Microsoft also said it’ll keep a close eye on feedback and may tweak the offering before the changes come in.

Cloud gaming has become an increasingly important part of the video game offering as the RAMpocalypse makes console gaming increasingly expensive. Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, recently predicted the video game industry will be in “commercial streaming mode” within three years — but for video game streaming to matter, it would have to run GTA 6 just as well as consoles do.

During an investor focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, Zelnick was asked for his thoughts on the video game industry as it buckles under the pressure of skyrocketing chip costs, which have forced Sony and Microsoft to raise the price of their consoles and potentially delay the launches of the PlayStation 6 and the next-gen Xbox, codenamed Project Helix.

Zelnick admitted the rising cost of hardware “is not a good thing,” because cheaper hardware means more hardware in people’s hands, which is what software companies desire. But he suggested the advent of video game streaming would go a long way to tackling this problem.

Both Sony and Microsoft are predicted to lean heavily on streaming in the coming years as they contend with the RAMpocalypse. “I just don't have any insight as to what the console manufacturers have planned, but it wouldn't at all surprise me if part of what they plan is streaming,” Zelnick offered.

In the shorter term, GTA 6 launches in November and it is expected to boost console sales significantly. And there are a number of use cases with cloud gaming that could make it a popular option for those either without a current gen console, or who are priced out of buying one. For example, Xbox Cloud Gaming is used by some Xbox One owners to play current gen games. It’s also used by some PC gamers to play games that are beyond their current machines. Some people use cloud gaming to sample Game Pass games before installing — although this of course won’t apply to GTA 6. Others use cloud gaming to extend playtime in rooms in which they don’t have a console — perhaps they’re at work or away over a weekend. So, while Microsoft may say GTA 6 has nothing to do with the November changes to Xbox cloud gaming, it’s hard to see past the timing here.

As for the price of cloud gaming time, don’t expect a ‘pay as you go’ system — Microsoft will sell batches of hours, and those hours won’t expire. That means there’s no pressure to use your hours before they disappear.

In July, Microsoft launched a test for ad-supported Xbox game streaming, promising the ads wouldn’t interrupt gameplay. “For many players, the device they already own now allows them to stream games with Xbox,” Microsoft said at the time. “Cloud can also help Xbox One owners play newer games built for Xbox Series X|S without needing to purchase new hardware right away. That can be especially meaningful in places where consoles are harder to find or less affordable, giving more players another way to access great games on devices they already have.”

The test of ad-supported Xbox streaming arrived amid console price rises that are pushing some gaming hardware towards the $1,000 mark. In June, Microsoft announced significant price rises for Xbox consoles, blaming the ongoing “components crisis.”

“Last October, we increased Xbox console price by 20-70 in the U.S.,” Microsoft said at the time. “We hoped another price increase would not be necessary, and we have spent the last several months working with suppliers on options. Unfortunately, console storage and memory prices have increased by more than 2.5x and we expect another doubling by the fall of 2027.

"The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles. Unlike phones, computers, speakers, and other consumer devices, consoles are typically not sold at a profit, but instead for less than they cost to make.”

New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

items.title: The New Hauntingly Twisted LEGO Mayor Manor Set Gets a Surprise First Discount at Walmart
items.author: Jacob Kienlen
items.content:
Spooky season is just around the corner, and one of the latest LEGO Halloween sets is already getting a discount. Walmart's Bricktember Sale is bringing the first price cut on the hauntingly twisted Mayor Manor set today.

Mayor Manor is part of a new line of creepy sets called the Midnight Valley Collection. It's basically a haunted house with oddly angled architecture and glow-in-the-dark minifigures. Seeing as it just came out on September 1, the fact that it's already getting a discount at Walmart is a very welcome surprise.

I am personally a big fan of LEGO's Architecture line of sets, so this particular build really appeals to me. Mostly because of the amount of thought that seems to have gone into making it feel haunted. LEGO bricks, by design, are usually perfectly aligned with each other. But the Mayor Manor utilizes its bricks in such a way that everything looks just a little bit crooked. It gives the mansion a rather haunted look without having to resort to things like boarded up windows or a crumbling façade.

The Mayor Manor is also designated as an 18+ set, so it's meant for adults to build and display. At just over 1,400 pieces, it's decently sized and comes with a ton of little details inside and outside of the house. In addition to the spooky exterior, you get to build the gothic decor of the inside of the home as well. All-in-all, it's an excellent display piece for Halloween with some cool surprises for anone who gets to build it. You also get three glow-in-the-dark minifigures, a cat, and a rat that you can display anywhere on the set.

More LEGO Halloween Sets on Sale

Some of the best Labor Day sales right now are on spooky-themed LEGO sets. I wrote earlier this week about the 3-in-1 Haunted Mansion set that dropped to a new low price, and that set is still on sale now. It isn't nearly as magnificent as the Mayor Manor set, but it does offer alternate builds like the Haunted Train and Haunted Ship that make it cool to put together. Since it isn't an 18+ set, it's also a little bit easier to build.

The other discount that dropped recently is on the popular Nightmare Before Christmas set. This build is based on Tim Burton's classic stop-motion film featuring Jack Skellington as he discovers the joys of Christmas. This is the first major price drop this set has received and it's absolutely worth picking up if your a fan of the movie.

items.title: After Years of Mocking the DC Flop, Ryan Reynolds Now Says ‘I Owe Everything’ to Green Lantern
items.description: After years of poking fun at Green Lantern, Ryan Reynolds admitted he owes his career and personal life to the infamous 2011 DC superhero movie.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Ryan Reynolds has spent over a decade mocking his notorious 2011 comic book movie flop, Green Lantern, perhaps most famously by including a meta post-credits scene in Deadpool 2 where the merc with a mouth goes back in time to blow out Reynolds’ brains all over a copy of the Green Lantern screenplay. Now, with the HBO series Lanterns out, the actor seems to have developed an appreciation for his DC film, declaring, “I owe my entire career to that movie.”

Speaking on the red carpet at the premiere of his new movie Mayday, Reynolds was asked by Entertainment Tonight if he’d ever consider making a cameo in Lanterns.

"I would totally do a cameo in that," Reynolds said. "I love it. I learned so much making that movie. And I know what you're thinking, you're thinking, 'Oh, learned what not to do.' In part, yes. But also, any time you're making something that large, there are core lessons that come of it.”

“I owe my entire career to that movie. I owe everything to that,” Reynolds said. “Everything about it was a gift that keeps on giving. And I really enjoyed the experience of making it."

Reynolds also met his wife, Blake Lively, on that film. He played Hal Jordan opposite Lively as played Carol Ferris.

Reynolds’ history of poking fun at Green Lantern is lengthy, including trolling fans that his Green Lantern was in the Snyder Cut. Green Lantern director Martin Campbell has expressed his regrets about the film, but thinks it “would’ve been great” had Reynolds scripted it.

Reynolds most recently popped up in a grey Deadpool costume at San Diego Comic-Con to crash the Avengers: Doomsday panel.

As for Lanterns, read our review and recap of the latest episode and discover why the showrunner altered John Stewart’s origin for it.

items.title: Sonic Creative Officer Takashi Iizuka Explains How Sega Found a Loophole to Let Sonic Shoot Enemies in Fortnite
items.description: Takashi Iizuka, a key figure in Sega’s Sonic Franchise, told IGN’s Jeffrey Vega about the unique difficulty the company faced in giving the Blue Blur a playable skin in Fortnite.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Takashi Iizuka, a key figure in Sega’s Sonic Franchise, told IGN’s Jeffrey Vega about the unique difficulty the company faced in giving the Blue Blur a playable skin in Fortnite.

While Shadow is somewhat famous for being an edgy, pistol-toting anti-hero, Sonic is a totally different character. The yang to Shadow’s yin, Sonic is an upbeat hedgehog who uses his extremely fast speed (and occasionally, the power of the Chaos Emeralds) to take down enemies.

That’s why Sega balked when it was first approached by Epic games with the idea of giving Shadow and Sonic their own Fortnite skins, according to Sonic Creative Officer Takashi Iizuka. Luckily, they were able to come up with a creative solution: Why not make a new Sonic variant?

“Epic Games came and spoke with us a couple years ago about putting Sonic in Fortnite, but Sonic is a character that will never hold a gun,” he told us. “And when thinking about the design of Fortnite, it was really hard to think about Sonic being in the game. But this time, we were able to take creative liberties and created Android Sonic.”

In the same vein as Metal Sonic, the team cooked up an Android version of the character that would be realistically capable of using a shotgun, thus allowing a variant of Sonic to be the one doing the shooting as a clever workaround.

“Because we made this Android version of Sonic, we were able to get this Android Sonic into Fortnite, have him hold a gun, and have him be able to really play inside Fortnite and be integrated into the game,” Iizuka explained.

This week's Shop is going full adventure mode 👀 pic.twitter.com/thT6CMd7Vq

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) August 20, 2026

Of course, this meant changing his design a bit in order for him to fit within the game — most notably, giving him longer legs.

“One of the things that’s really important in Fortnite is to be able to have all the weapons and items and things to be used amongst all the different characters. So, if we had our regular version of Sonic in there, it really wouldn’t work. Like, you couldn't use all the items and things to apply to your character,” he continued.

“We needed to have a character shape that is similar to all the other Fortnite characters. That was something that Epic Games said was really important, that we need to make sure we have the same shapes as all the other characters. And from there, it was really working with the Epic Games team on making sure the Android version really felt like a Sonic character but still fit the requirements of what the body proportions and shapes needed to be.”

Sonic, Shadow, Tails, Knuckles, and even Dr. Eggman are available in Fortnite, along with a new area modeled after Green Hill Zone. You can check out more from our interview with Takashi Iizuka, or catch up on the latest Fortnite news here.
